reason: I want to examine the channel grains, so collecting them in a jar seems like a natural first step.
expectation: I expect to collect a sample of the channel material for closer inspection.

alternatives.reason: The hammer could expose the rock face, but I want to start with the loose grains.

effect: The sediment is collected, so I can inspect it now.
reaction: That worked as expected; I am curious what the grains reveal.
reason: The hand lens should let me examine the collected grains.
expectation: I expect to see details of their shapes or composition.

effect: The rounded grains suggest movement and wear but do not identify the carrier; I will investigate the ledge next.
reaction: I like the cautious comparison with the earlier angular grains; it makes the observation meaningful without overstating it.
reason: The hammer is the remaining offered combination and should expose the rock surface.
expectation: I expect to chip the ledge and reveal fresh rock.

effect: I have a chip to prepare, rather than an examined face yet.
reaction: The chip is a plausible intermediate step, though it provides no detail yet.
reason: The only offered combination uses the abrasive pad to prepare the chip for inspection.
expectation: I expect to smooth or clean a surface so its layers are easier to see.

effect: The prepared face reveals bands and a crosscutting vein, giving another geological observation alongside the pebbles.
reaction: The vein cutting across the bands makes me curious about their relative history, though the chapter leaves that open.

mostWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the channel grains was most worthwhile: comparing rounded grains with the earlier angular sample suggests wear while leaving the carrier uncertain.

leastWorthwhile.text: Taking the rock chip was a straightforward intermediate action with no detail on its own; it felt less engaging than inspecting the results.

surprise.text: The pale vein cutting across the bands raised a question about the rock's history that I did not anticipate.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless: collecting, looking, chipping and smoothing all had understandable physical purposes, though the latter two were the only offered gameplay choices at their turns.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to learn whether later evidence helps explain the worn grains and the vein, although the choices here were mostly straightforward.
